categories.main_business_segments: Elastic operates as a single reportable segment focused on its Search AI Platform, which underpins three primary solutions: Elasticsearch (search applications), Elastic Observability (IT monitoring and analytics), and Elastic Security (cybersecurity analytics and protection). These solutions are available as both cloud-based services and self-managed software, serving a wide range of use cases across industries.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: Elastic’s core technology is the Elasticsearch distributed, real-time vector database and analytics engine, capable of ingesting, storing, searching, and analyzing structured and unstructured data at scale. The platform integrates advanced AI and machine learning, including native vector search, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), anomaly detection, and support for large language models (LLMs). Development is driven by an open software model, with a single code base maintained across cloud and self-managed deployments.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Elastic serves organizations of all sizes, including enterprises, educational institutions, and government entities, across over 125 countries. Its key customer segments include IT, security, and developer teams seeking solutions for search, observability, and security use cases. Major end markets include technology, financial services, government, e-commerce, and telecommunications.
categories.geographic_coverage: Elastic has a global presence, with customers in over 125 countries and employees in more than 40 countries. The United States accounts for 56% of revenue, while the rest of the world contributes 44%. The company’s cloud services are available across major public cloud providers in more than 55 regions worldwide.
categories.supply_chain_position: Elastic operates downstream in the software supply chain, providing end-user solutions and platforms directly to organizations and through partners. It does not manufacture hardware or provide raw data infrastructure, but rather delivers software and cloud services that enable customers to manage and analyze their own data.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Elastic’s strategic priorities center on extending product leadership in AI-powered search, observability, and security, with significant ongoing investment in R&D (approximately $366 million in FY25). Key innovation themes include generative AI integration, vector search, cloud-native and serverless offerings, and expanding ease of use and developer engagement. The company also pursues selective acquisitions to enhance technology and market reach.
categories.revenue_model: Elastic primarily generates revenue through paid subscriptions for its cloud-based and self-managed software offerings, using resource-based and consumption-based pricing models. Subscriptions account for 93% of total revenue, with additional revenue from consulting and training services. The company also offers free tiers and features to drive adoption and conversion to paid subscriptions.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Elastic faces competition from open source and commercial search platforms (e.g., Apache Solr, Lucidworks, MongoDB Atlas, Algolia, Pinecone), observability vendors (Datadog, Splunk, Dynatrace, New Relic), security vendors (CrowdStrike, Palo Alto Networks, Microsoft Sentinel), and cloud providers offering forked versions of its software. Elastic differentiates itself with a unified, extensible platform and broad use case coverage, but many competitors have greater resources and brand recognition.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For the fiscal year ended April 30, 2025, Elastic reported $1.48 billion in revenue (17% YoY growth), with approximately 21,500 customers and over 1,510 customers generating more than $100,000 in annual contract value. The company recorded a net loss of $108 million in FY25, following a net income of $62 million in FY24 and a net loss of $236 million in FY23. Elastic maintains strong cash reserves ($1.4 billion) and continues to invest heavily in growth.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Elastic’s value proposition lies in its ability to deliver real-time, scalable, and highly relevant search and analytics across diverse data types, powered by advanced AI and machine learning. The platform’s speed, flexibility, extensibility, and open development model enable rapid innovation and broad adoption. Elastic emphasizes unified deployment across cloud and on-premises, developer-centric tools, and integrated solutions for search, observability, and security as key differentiators.
